title: The fraction field of a smooth domain is separable over the base field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a nonzero commutative integral domain with a $k$-algebra structure, and let $F$ be a field of fractions of $A$: the map $A\hookrightarrow F$ is injective and every element of $F$ is $a/b$ for $a,b\in A$, $b\ne0$. Give $F$ the induced $k$-algebra structure [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume $k\to A$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then $F/k$ is separable in the nonalgebraic sense [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every intermediate field $k\subseteq E\subseteq F$ finitely generated as a field over $k$ has a transcendence basis over $k$ over which $E$ is separable algebraic.

source.place: Tag 037X, lemma-localization-smooth-separable, implication localization of a smooth algebra implies separable; also Tag 07ND, lemma-smooth-at-generic-point, forward implication with R = k and S = A.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable] to the given field extension $F/k$; this proves exactly the desired assertion. Otherwise the characteristic of the field $k$ is a prime $p>0$. Work in this case for the remaining steps.

source.place: Tag 07ND, lemma-smooth-at-generic-point, forward implication, with the characteristic-zero case made explicit using Tag 00TX, lemma-characteristic-zero-local-smooth, proof, first sentence

proof.text: Let $L/k$ be an arbitrary field extension and set $B=L\otimes_k A$, with multiplication $(\lambda\otimes a)(\mu\otimes b)=\lambda\mu\otimes ab$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] to $k\to A$ and $k\to L$: the map $L\to B$ is smooth. Apply [lem-sc-smooth-algebra-reduced-field] over the field $L$ to conclude that $B$ is reduced. No perfectness of $k$ or $L$ is assumed, and $B$ is not asserted to be a domain.

source.place: Tag 07ND, lemma-smooth-at-generic-point, forward proof: base change to any field extension gives a smooth, hence reduced algebra; base change is Tag 00T4, lemma-base-change-smooth; reducedness is the consequence used there of Tag 00TT, lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field (also varieties.tex, Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal)

proof.text: Put $S=A\setminus\{0\}$, a multiplicative subset since $A$ is a nonzero domain. The given fractions identify $F$ with $S^{-1}A$: $a/s\mapsto a/s\in F$ is surjective by hypothesis and injective since $A\hookrightarrow F$ is injective and $s\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with base ring $k$, algebra $A$, multiplicative subset $S$, module $M=A$ and $N=L$. It identifies $S^{-1}(A\otimes_k L)$ with $F\otimes_k L$ by $(a\otimes\lambda)/s\mapsto(a/s)\otimes\lambda$. The swap $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes\lambda$ identifies $B$ with $A\otimes_k L$; both maps preserve products and units, as the formulas on pure tensors show. Thus $F\otimes_k L$ is the localization of the reduced ring $B$ at the images of $S$. Explicitly, if $(b/s)^n=0$ with $n\ge1$, the zero criterion for fractions gives $t\in S$ with $t b^n=0$ in $B$. Then $(tb)^n=t^{n-1}(t b^n)=0$, so $tb=0$ by reducedness of $B$, and hence $b/s=0$. Here $s,t$ act through $A\to B$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. This proves reducedness of $F\otimes_k L$ for every $L/k$.

source.place: Tag 07ND, lemma-smooth-at-generic-point, forward proof, passage to the fraction field; Tag 04KN, lemma-geometrically-reduced-permanence, localization clause and its two hints written out; tensor-localization formula from Tags 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization, and 00D2, lemma-tensor-with-bimodule

proof.text: Now $k$ has characteristic the prime $p>0$, $F/k$ is a field extension with the specified induced structure, and step 3 proves that $F\otimes_k L$ is reduced for every field extension $L/k$. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-reduced-extension-separable], so $F/k$ is separable. By clause (2) of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], this means that every intermediate field $k\subseteq E\subseteq F$ finitely generated over $k$ has a transcendence basis over which $E$ is separable algebraic. Together with step 1 this proves the assertion in all characteristics.
